# Study design

The estimand is the population marginal risk difference
\(E[Y(1)]-E[Y(0)]\). A denotes binary exposure, Y the binary outcome, X the
observed covariates, and R = 1 an observed exposure. Each method/design cell
has 500 Monte Carlo attempts. Sample sizes are 500, 1,000 and 2,000.

## Gaussian-covariate families

For Families 1–5, \(X_1,X_2,X_3\) are independent standard normal variables.
Exposure and outcome are generated from

\[
\operatorname{logit}P(A=1\mid X)=-0.2+0.9X_1+X_2+0.8X_3,
\]
\[
\operatorname{logit}P(Y=1\mid A,X)=0.7+A+0.5X_1+0.9X_2+0.7X_3
 +\gamma_{\mathrm{int}}A(X_1+X_2+X_3).
\]

Under MAR, the exposure observation model is
\[
\operatorname{logit}P(R=1\mid X,Y)=\alpha+0.6X_1+0.7X_2+0.8X_3+\gamma_Y Y.
\]
Under MCAR it is constant, with \(\alpha=\operatorname{logit}(1-s)\), where
s is the missing exposure share. MAR intercepts are calibrated with 200,000
draws. The true marginal risk difference is integrated using 1,000,000 draws.

| Family | Variation |
|---|---|
| `missing_share` | s = 0.2, 0.4, 0.5, 0.6; MAR |
| `gamma_y` | \(\gamma_Y\) = 0, 0.5, 0.8; MAR |
| `outcome_interaction` | \(\gamma_{\mathrm{int}}\) = 0, 0.5, 1; MAR |
| `missing_mechanism` | MCAR and MAR |
| `outcome_interaction_mcar` | \(\gamma_{\mathrm{int}}\) = 0, 0.5, 1; MCAR |

Main-effects and interaction GLMs are compared. The interaction outcome model
contains \(A(X_1+X_2+X_3)\); the imputation model includes Y-by-covariate
terms. The treatment propensity model has main effects. Scenario 3 also
includes RF specifications.

## Nonlinear covariates

Scenario 6 (`nonlinear_binary`, DGP `ks_binary_v1`) generates independent
standard normal \(Z_1,Z_2,Z_3\), but estimators observe only
\[
X_1=e^{Z_1/2},\qquad X_2=\frac{Z_2}{1+e^{Z_1}}+10,\qquad
X_3=\left(\frac{Z_1Z_3}{25}+0.6\right)^3.
\]
The generating models are
\[
\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{logit}P(A=1\mid Z)&=0.3-0.8Z_1+0.8Z_2-0.25Z_3,\\
\operatorname{logit}P(Y=1\mid A,Z)&=1+2A+0.5Z_1+Z_2+0.5Z_3+\eta Z_1Z_2,\\
\operatorname{logit}P(R=1\mid Z,Y)&=\alpha+0.5Z_1-0.5Z_2+0.25Z_3+0.5Y.
\end{aligned}
\]

The manuscript and included data use η = 1 (code variable `gamma_int`, cells
7–9), MAR and 40% missing exposure. The runner also supports η = 0 and 0.5.
Here η is a covariate–covariate interaction. The observation intercept is
calibrated using 200,000 draws; the true marginal risk difference uses
2,000,000 draws. It is not the coefficient of A in the outcome model.

# Estimators and inference

Complete-data AIPW uses exposure before missingness; complete-case AIPW uses
only observed exposures. Single-imputation AIPW treats one completed exposure
vector as observed. MICE AIPW pools the ten completed-data analyses. MR has
code identifier `drcmd` and calls `drcmd::drcmd()`. TR-AIPW (`tr_aipw`) is a
separate additional analysis with GLM specifications.

| Scenario 6 component | GLM specification | RF specification |
|---|---|---|
| Single imputation | Logistic probabilities, Bernoulli draws | RF probabilities, Bernoulli draws |
| MICE | `method = "logreg"` | `method = "rf"`, `ntree = 500` |
| AIPW outcome regression | GLM | RF |
| AIPW propensity | Main-effects logistic | Main-effects logistic |

Exposure imputation uses Y, X1, X2 and X3. Both MICE branches use 10
imputations and 10 iterations. RF-MICE in Scenario 3 also uses 500 trees
with the ranger backend. AIPW uses 10 outer cross-fitting folds and 9 internal
SuperLearner CV folds. MR uses 10 outer and 5 internal folds; its RF
specification uses RF outcome and pseudo-outcome regressions, with GLM
treatment and observation models. SuperLearner forests use 500 trees.
AIPW and MR use probability bounds of 0.025 and 0.975.

For imputation estimates Q and variances U, Rubin pooling uses
\[
\bar Q=\operatorname{mean}(Q),\quad \bar U=\operatorname{mean}(U),\quad
B=\operatorname{var}(Q),\quad T=\bar U+(1+1/m)B.
\]
The 95% interval is \(\bar Q\pm t_{0.975,\nu}\sqrt T\), with
\(r=(1+1/m)B/\bar U\) and \(\nu=(m-1)(1+1/r)^2\).
When B is at most machine precision, \(\nu=\infty\). Pooling omits nonfinite
Q/U pairs and negative variances; fewer than two usable imputations give no
SE or interval. Both Scenario 6 branches use this same rule.

AIPW and MR use influence-curve standard errors and normal intervals.
TR-AIPW uses 100 bootstrap resamples, requires at least 80 valid estimates,
and reports their SD and percentile interval (quantile type 1). Its inverse
weights are shrunk at the 99th percentile. Bootstrap estimates must satisfy
the intervention-risk and risk-difference bounds.

# Results and failures

Bias is mean(estimate − truth); RMSE is the square root of the mean squared
error; Monte Carlo SD is the sample SD; mean SE averages estimated SEs.
Coverage includes both interval endpoints. Families 1–5 omit missing values
separately for each metric. Scenario 6 report summaries require a finite
estimate, nonnegative SE, ordered finite interval and successful status.
Failure rates below use joint validity for every family. Failed attempts
remain in the denominator. Some failed fits have no recorded diagnostic.

```{r failure-counts}
kable(failures |> group_by(family) |> summarise(Attempts=sum(n_attempted),
  Valid=sum(n_valid),Failed=sum(n_failed),.groups="drop"),
  caption="Recorded attempts and joint estimate/SE/interval validity.")
```

```{r results, results='asis'}
for (family in names(tables)) {
  x <- tables[[family]]
  cat("\n\n## ",family_names[[family]],"\n\n",sep="")
  cat("Operating characteristics at n = ",params$table_n,".\n\n",sep="")
  cols <- intersect(c("target_missing_share","gamma_y","gamma_int","missing_mechanism",
    "method","nuisance_spec","bias","mc_sd","mean_se","rmse","coverage"),names(x))
  print(kable(x[x$n==params$table_n,cols],digits=4,row.names=FALSE))
  cat("\n\n")
  z <- x |> mutate(Method=factor(method,levels=names(method_labels),labels=unname(method_labels))) |>
    pivot_longer(c(bias,rmse,coverage),names_to="Metric",values_to="value")
  # The report shows all included designs; the manuscript script applies its specified filters.
  print(ggplot(z,aes(Method,value,color=nuisance_spec))+
    geom_point(position=position_dodge(width=.5))+
    facet_grid(Metric~n,scales="free_y")+coord_flip()+theme_bw()+
    labs(x=NULL,y=NULL,color="Specification"))
  cat("\n\n")
}
```

# Manuscript comparisons

`scripts/manuscript_figures.R` generates the three manuscript PDFs and PNGs:
interaction under MCAR/MAR at n = 2,000; outcome dependence under MAR at
n = 2,000; and nonlinear covariates at η = 1 across all three sample sizes.
The first comparison uses main-effects and interaction GLMs; the second uses
main-effects GLMs; the third uses the logistic/GLM and RF/RF imputation
branches specified above. TR-AIPW and Scenario 3 RF sensitivity analyses are
not included in those comparisons.

Figure summaries count valid point estimates and intervals separately and
export their numerical values and denominators. They do not discard finite
outliers. Changing both imputation and outcome regression in the nonlinear
comparison means differences cannot be attributed solely to the outcome model.

The full-data benchmark still estimates its nuisance functions, and transformed
covariates can misspecify GLMs even with complete exposure. Complete-case
selection under MAR can change the target population. Single-imputation
standard errors omit imputation uncertainty. Interpret interval coverage
alongside failure rates, bias and Monte Carlo variability.
